answer: Each identity registers one relic at a forge vertex, locks 80 credit, and pays 45 credit for a laboratory assay of its vertex lattice and forge mark. The assay enters a public book and marks the relic spent, so a second identity with the same relic loses its bond, while an honest identity keeps its bond on one matching assay. A rented-relic ring fails because the rented relic is already recorded and the second assay burns the bond. The k-th fake pays 125, so 1,000 fakes lock 125,000 credit with no shared assay, and anyone can recompute an assay from the forge book at that vertex.
